title: Normal force magnitude
description: Essential: The student's final answer for part (1) must correctly state the normal force as 35 N (or equivalent).

title: Frictional force magnitude
description: Essential: The student's final answer for part (1) must correctly state the static friction force as 5√3 N (or equivalent decimal).

title: Vertical force balance reasoning
description: Important: The solution must apply Newton's first law in the vertical direction, correctly resolving F into components (N = mg - F sin θ).

title: Horizontal force balance reasoning
description: Important: The solution must apply Newton's first law in the horizontal direction, equating friction to the horizontal component of F (f = F cos θ).

title: Friction at impending motion
description: Important: For part (2), the solution must state that at the point of sliding, the horizontal force component equals the maximum static friction (F₀ cos θ = μ N₀).

title: Normal force at increased F
description: Important: For part (2), the solution must correctly calculate the new normal force when F=20 N using vertical equilibrium (N₀ = mg - F₀ sin θ).

title: Coefficient of friction
description: Essential: The student's final answer for part (2) must correctly give the coefficient of kinetic friction as √3/3 (or equivalent decimal/numeric form).

title: Sign error in normal force
description: Pitfall: Penalize if the student incorrectly adds the vertical component of F to the weight when calculating the normal force (e.g., N = mg + F sin θ).

title: Unit omission or misuse
description: Pitfall: Penalize if final numerical answers for forces lack units (N) or if the coefficient is given with incorrect units.
